title: Using Multiple Nullable Fields for Disjoint States
damaged_code:
```rust
struct Task {
    id: u64,
    assigned_worker: Option<String>,
    completion_date: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
    rejection_reason: Option<String>,
}
```
pattern: Defining a struct with multiple optional (`Option`) fields that represent disjoint, mutually exclusive states.
why_bad: It allows representing impossible states (e.g., having both a `completion_date` and a `rejection_reason` simultaneously). Upstream and downstream components must write complex match patterns to resolve the true state.
detection: Structs containing 3 or more `Option` fields that are semantically tied to mutually exclusive lifecycle phases of the struct.
counterexample:
A struct with truly independent, non-exclusive optional fields:
```rust
struct UserSettings {
    theme: Option<Theme>,
    timezone: Option<TimeZone>,
}
```
fix:
Define a clean state enum carrying only the relevant data inside each variant.
```rust
enum TaskState {
    Assigned { worker: String },
    Completed { date: DateTime<Utc> },
    Rejected { reason: String },
}
```
source: *Domain Modeling made Functional* by Scott Wlaschin (p. 108).
